text:
alex: kicked off an nsys + perfetto capture on dedicated-a100 (llama-13b, int8, seq=2048, batch=8). seeing ~25% regression vs baseline. timeline points to many short kernels around attention/KV paths.

maria: can you paste the top-kernel breakdown from the nsys summary? trying to understand if it's compute-bound or launch/mem-bound.

alex: nsys top kernels by total GPU time:
- kv_fuse_update_kernel ........ 31.7% GPU time, achieved_occ ~12%
- matmul_128x128_tn ............ 22.5% GPU time, achieved_occ ~16%
- softmax_long_seq_kernel ...... 8.6% GPU time, occ ~8%
- kv_memmove_prefetch .......... 7.1% GPU time
- cudaStreamWaitEvent (sync) ... 4.9% (lots of host-device waits)

chris: low achieved occupancy + high GPU time usually == many small kernels or high shared/reg usage per block. any per-kernel launch dims/counters?

alex: grabbed perfetto snippets. examples:
```
matmul_128x128_tn: grid=(1536,1,1) block=(256,1,1) time=1.6ms
kv_fuse_update_kernel: grid=(896,1,1) block=(128,1,1) time=2.2ms
```
perf counters show L2 load stalls and high DRAM request latency on matmul.

sam: question: are these kernels being invoked multiple times per token when KV cache hits occur? that would fragment work.

alex: yes. perfetto zoom at request shows attention op splits into: kv_prefetch -> small matmul -> kv_pack -> kv_write -> cudaEvent sync. That's ~5-7 small kernels per token for cached prefixes.

maria: that fragmentation would trash tensor core utilization. kernel launch overhead + small grids -> SMs idle.

jin: two vectors: 1) reduce number of launches by fusing adjacent ops, 2) increase per-kernel tile size for long sequences so each launch does more work. Also consider cublasLt path for batched matmuls.

chris: also verify resource usage per block. NCU shows kv_fuse_update uses ~44KB shared mem and ~64 regs/thread, limiting resident warps to ~10%.

sam: maybe the KV prefetch logic is over-eager: I see cudaMemPrefetchAsync spikes before many small kernels. If prefetch happens per-token instead of per-chunk, we pay mem traffic and latency.

alex: plan proposed:
1) capture targeted nsys with --capture-range to isolate single request window and export ncu counters (sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy, l2_hit_rate)
2) prototype a reduced-shared-mem variant (split reduction) for kv_fuse_update to raise occupancy
3) try matmul fallback using cublasLt for contiguous batched matmuls
4) add selector logging: tile_size chosen, fallback flag, reason (regs/shared/accuracy)

maria: +1. also create a synthetic unit test that mimics 90% KV-hit pattern so we can iterate quickly on changes.

chris: I can run a tuner sweep overnight on dev A100: tile sizes [64,128,256], thread-block dims, and measure avg kernel time + sm_efficiency.

jin: for step 2, try lowering per-block shared mem and moving intermediate reduction to global memory if bandwidth allows. trades latency for occupancy but may reduce overall GPU time.

alex: will start traces now and post perfetto links/time windows. focusing on the 00:07-00:08 range where prefix storm is visible. also capturing ncu csvs.

perf-bot: [perf job] run-#512 completed on a100-dev-1, artifacts at /srv/perf/1780501234/

alex: thanks all, posting traces and initial ncu CSVs in a follow-up message. reconvene after tuner and prototype runs. :thumbsup:
